mainTopic: Accepting returning sinners, the days around the festivals of עובדי כוכבים, the rejected rulings of נחום המדי, and the order of praise and requests in prayer
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about people who return after doing wrong. רבי שמעון and רבי יהושע בן קרחה say they are accepted back even if they sinned in public, and רבי יוחנן rules like them. A new משנה follows. רבי ישמעאל forbids business with עובדי כוכבים three days before and three days after their festivals, while the חכמים forbid only the days before. The גמרא gives four possible ways the חכמים differ from the תנא קמא of the first משנה. The last of these involves נחום המדי, who forbids only one day before. This leads to a series of rulings by נחום המדי that the חכמים rejected with the words 'let the matter be forgotten.' Each time, a תנא who seems to agree with him turns out to hold something different. אביי points to one ruling of his that we follow: asking for personal needs in שומע תפלה. רב אחא answers that this idea goes back to a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about whether requests or prayer come first. The גמרא traces that dispute to רבי שמלאי's rule, learned from משה רבינו, that praise of ה׳ comes before personal requests.

steps.title: Those who sinned in public are not accepted back
steps.stepSummary: The end of an opinion in a ברייתא: people who returned after doing wrong in public are not accepted back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they did it in public, we do not accept them back.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that started before this section. The opinion here says that if these people did their wrongdoing openly, we do not accept them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of this opinion (רבי יהודה's) said that people who sinned privately can be accepted back. This line adds the other half: sinning in public is treated more harshly. This sets up the disagreement that comes next.

phrases.english: If they did it in public, we do not accept them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who sinned in public are not accepted back.

steps.title: Penitents are always accepted, public or private
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון and רבי יהושע בן קרחה say we accept them back either way, based on a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון and רבי יהושע בן קרחה say: in both cases we accept them, as the פסוק says, "Return, you wayward children."
steps.whatsHappening: Two תנאים disagree with the previous opinion. They hold that whether the wrongdoing was private or public, the person is accepted back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their source is a פסוק in which God calls even the wayward children to come back. If God welcomes them back, so should we, no matter how open the sin was.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha say:
Either way, we accept them,
As it says: "Return, you wayward children."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:22

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Penitents are accepted whether they sinned in private or in public.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון and רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows the pair who accept penitents in all cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק of the village of עכו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows that pair.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא steps in to decide the dispute. The final ruling is that we accept people back even if they sinned in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "That pair" means רבי שמעון and רבי יהושע בן קרחה. So the practical law is the more welcoming view.
steps.whatToRemember: Someone who truly returns is accepted back, even if he sinned in public. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון and רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak, a man of the village of Akko, said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows that pair.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתָא כְּאוֹתוֹ הַזּוּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions in steps 1 and 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Penitents are accepted regardless of whether their sin was public.

steps.title: The new משנה: which days around their festivals are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל forbids business three days before and after the festivals of עובדי כוכבים. The חכמים forbid only the days before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: three days before them and three days after them, business is forbidden. The חכמים say: before their festivals it is forbidden, after their festivals it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a dispute about which days around the festivals of עובדי כוכבים a Jew may not do business with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל adds three days after the festival to the forbidden time. The חכמים say the time after the festival is permitted, and only the days before are forbidden.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Yishmael says:
Three days before them and three days after them, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: "Them" means their festivals, and the forbidden thing is doing business with them.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Before their festivals, it is forbidden,
After their festivals, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the previous topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: three days before and after are forbidden. חכמים: only before is forbidden.

steps.title: By רבי ישמעאל's count, business with a נוצרי is always forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל points out that according to רבי ישמעאל, business with a נוצרי is forbidden every day of the week.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא בר אבדימי said in the name of שמואל: a נוצרי, according to רבי ישמעאל, is always forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a practical consequence of רבי ישמעאל's view. If a group's festival comes every week, his rule forbids every single day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their festival day comes every week. Three days before it plus three days after it, together with the day itself, cover the whole week. So by רבי ישמעאל's count, business with them would never be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi said that Shmuel said:
A Christian, according to Rabbi Yishmael,
is always forbidden.
phrases.notes: His festival day comes every Sunday, so three days on each side fill the entire week.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from רבי ישמעאל's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, business with a נוצרי is forbidden all week.

steps.title: Aren't the חכמים saying the same as the first תנא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים of our משנה and asks how they differ from the תנא קמא of the first משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "The חכמים say: before their festivals it is forbidden, after their festivals it is permitted." But the חכמים are the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the חכמים' line from the משנה and raises a problem. Their view sounds identical to what the first משנה of the מסכת already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה (on 2a) already taught that the three days before their festivals are forbidden, and it said nothing about the days after. So the חכמים here seem to add nothing new, and the גמרא wants to know what the real difference is.

phrases.english: "And the Sages say:
Before their festivals it is forbidden,
after their festivals it is permitted, etc."
The Sages are the same as the first tanna!
phrases.notes: This means the anonymous opinion in the very first משנה of the מסכת, which forbids three days before their festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲכָמִים הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי ישמעאל's view to the חכמים' view in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the חכמים in our משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their view appears identical to the תנא קמא of the first משנה, so a separate opinion seems unnecessary.

steps.title: They differ on whether the festival day counts in the three days
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא counts three days not including the festival. The later חכמים count the festival day as one of the three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is "them without their festivals." The תנא קמא holds the three days are without the festivals. The later Rabbis hold the three days include the festivals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two views are not the same. They disagree about how to count the three forbidden days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, there are three full forbidden days before the festival, not counting the festival itself. For the later חכמים, the festival day is one of the three, so only two days before it are forbidden. The two views look alike, but their counts come out different.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
The days themselves, without their festivals

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sets of "חכמים." The תנא קמא is the opinion in the first משנה of the מסכת, and the "later Rabbis" are the חכמים in our משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא counts three days before the festival, not including it. The later חכמים include the festival day in the three.

phrases.english: "Them without their festivals" is the difference between them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the three days. The question is whether the festival day is counted as one of them.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: הֵן בְּלֹא אֵידֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: The first tanna holds: the days without their festivals,
And the later Rabbis hold: the days and their festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵן בְּלֹא אֵידֵיהֶן אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference in how the days are counted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים and the תנא קמא hold exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא counts three days apart from the festival. The later חכמים count the festival as one of the three.

steps.title: Second answer: business already done
steps.stepSummary: The difference is about someone who already did business. The תנא קמא permits benefit from the profits, and the later חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that they argue about someone who already did business. The first תנא holds that if he did business, the profits are permitted. The later חכמים hold that the profits are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question from Step 6. The two opinions argue about what happens after someone has already broken the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the difference was about how the days are counted. Here both sides may count the same way. They argue only about after the fact: may you keep and use the profits from forbidden business? The תנא קמא says yes, and the later חכמים say no.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say — introduces another possible answer
The later Rabbis — the חכמים quoted in the second משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This argument is not about whether you may do business ahead of time. Both sides agree you should not. They argue only about the profits once it already happened.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
the difference between them is one who already did business,

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: נָשָׂא וְנָתַן מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: the first tanna holds: if he did business, it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן בָּתְרָאֵי סָבְרִי: נָשָׂא וְנָתַן אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and the later Rabbis hold: if he did business, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: נָשָׂא וְנָתַן אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 6's question, instead of the counting difference from Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative point of argument (after the fact versus before)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two opinions seemed to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ on whether profits from business already done are permitted.

steps.title: Third answer: שמואל's ruling for the גולה
steps.stepSummary: The difference is about שמואל's rule that outside ארץ ישראל only the festival day itself is forbidden. The תנא קמא accepts it, and the later חכמים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that they argue about שמואל's rule. שמואל said that outside ארץ ישראל only their festival day itself is forbidden. The first תנא agrees with שמואל, and the later חכמים do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer: the two opinions argue about whether the lighter rule of שמואל for the גולה is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says that outside ארץ ישראל only the festival day itself is forbidden, not the days before it. According to this answer, the תנא קמא accepts that leniency, while the later חכמים forbid the days before the festival everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: In the Diaspora — outside ארץ ישראל
He holds of it / they do not hold of it

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: the difference between them is Shmuel's ruling,
as Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּגּוֹלָה אֵין אָסוּר אֶלָּא יוֹם אֵידָם,
phrases.english: in the Diaspora, only their festival day itself is forbidden,
the first tanna holds like Shmuel,
the later Rabbis do not hold like Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third separate answer to the question from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative point of argument (location: the גולה)
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא accepts שמואל's leniency for the גולה, and the later חכמים reject it.

steps.title: Fourth answer: the view of נחום המדי
steps.stepSummary: The difference is about נחום המדי, who forbids only one day before the festival. The later חכמים agree with him, and the תנא קמא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that they argue about נחום המדי's view. A ברייתא teaches that נחום המדי says only the one day before their festival is forbidden. The first תנא does not agree with נחום המדי, and the later חכמים do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth answer. The question is whether the forbidden time before the festival is only one day, as נחום המדי says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא clearly says three days, so he cannot agree with נחום המדי's one day. The later חכמים do not give a number, so the גמרא suggests they hold that only one day before is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּנַחוּם הַמָּדִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: If you wish, say: the difference between them is the view of Nachum the Mede.
As it is taught: Nachum the Mede says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד לִפְנֵי אֵידֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: it is forbidden only one day before their festivals,

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא לֵית לֵיהּ דְּנַחוּם הַמָּדִי,
phrases.english: the first tanna does not hold like Nachum the Mede,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן בָּתְרָאֵי אִית לְהוּ דְּנַחוּם הַמָּדִי.
phrases.english: and the later Rabbis do hold like Nachum the Mede.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּנַחוּם הַמָּדִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth separate answer to the question from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative point of argument (number of days)
steps.terutzMaskana: The later חכמים agree with נחום המדי's one day, and the תנא קמא does not.

steps.title: נחום המדי's ruling and the חכמים's rejection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes נחום המדי's ruling of only one day. The חכמים answer that his statement should be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself: נחום המדי says only one day before their festivals is forbidden. They said to him: this statement should be forgotten and not said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to look at נחום המדי's statement on its own. It shows that the other חכמים strongly rejected it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is now studying a source it just mentioned. The חכמים's harsh words show that one day is not the הלכה. This sets up the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself — now we look closely at the source just quoted

phrases.english: The matter itself: Nachum the Mede says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד לִפְנֵי אֵידֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: it is forbidden only one day before their festivals.
They said to him:
Let the matter be forgotten and not said.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, נַחוּם הַמָּדִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא quoted in Step 10 and studies it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחום המדי forbids only one day before, and the חכמים reject his view completely.

steps.title: But the later חכמים agree with him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can his view be called forgotten, when the later חכמים of our משנה seem to hold like him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the later חכמים who hold like him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים's rejection by pointing back to Step 10. There, the later חכמים of the משנה were said to agree with נחום המדי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a whole group of חכמים in a משנה holds this view, it cannot be called a forgotten statement. So either the rejection or the answer in Step 10 seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is — opens a challenge

phrases.english: But there are the later Rabbis, who hold like him!
phrases.notes: This points back to the fourth answer, where the later חכמים agreed with נחום המדי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא רַבָּנַן בָּתְרָאֵי דְּקָיְימִי כְּוָותֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in Step 11 using the answer from Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's statement that נחום המדי's view should be forgotten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view held by the later חכמים of a משנה cannot be called forgotten.

steps.title: Those חכמים are נחום המדי himself
steps.stepSummary: The 'חכמים' of the משנה are really נחום המדי. The rest of the חכמים disagree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are these חכמים? It is נחום המדי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The 'חכמים' in the משנה are just נחום המדי, so no larger group holds his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The title 'חכמים' sounds like a big group, but here it stands for one תנא, נחום המדי. So the other חכמים can still reject his view, and the fourth answer still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are the חכמים? — asks who is really behind the title

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gave four answers for how the later חכמים differ from the תנא קמא: how the days are counted, business already done, שמואל's rule for the גולה, and נחום המדי's one day. In the last answer, the 'חכמים' are really נחום המדי, whose view the other חכמים rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the word 'חכמים' always means the majority. Here it is a title for one תנא, נחום המדי.

phrases.english: Who are the Rabbis?
It is Nachum the Mede.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן חֲכָמִים? נַחוּם הַמָּדִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the speaker behind an unnamed title
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חכמים' meant a group of Rabbis who agreed with נחום המדי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'חכמים' is נחום המדי alone, and the other חכמים disagree with him.

steps.title: נחום המדי permits selling an old male horse in wartime
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes נחום המדי: one may sell non-Jews a male, old horse during war. The חכמים reject this and say it should be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: נחום המדי says one may sell them a male, old horse in wartime. They said to him: let this matter be forgotten and not be said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of נחום המדי that the חכמים rejected with the same phrase we saw in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחום המדי allows selling a horse only in a narrow case: it is male, old, and the time is war. The חכמים do not accept even this narrow allowance. This sets up the same kind of question the גמרא asked in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the matter be forgotten and not be said, meaning it is not the הלכה

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
Nachum the Mede says:
One may sell them a male horse
and an old one, during a war.
They said to him:
Let the matter be forgotten and not be said.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: נַחוּם הַמָּדִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another ruling of נחום המדי that was rejected in the same way as the one in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחום המדי permits selling a male, old horse to non-Jews in wartime; the חכמים reject it.

steps.title: But בן בתירא also permits selling a horse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can this be called forgotten, when בן בתירא in a משנה also permits selling a horse?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is בן בתירא who agrees with him, as we learned in a משנה: בן בתירא permits selling a horse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that נחום המדי's view is 'forgotten,' because a תנא in a משנה seems to hold the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a view appears in a משנה, it is not forgotten. Since בן בתירא allows selling a horse, it looks like נחום המדי has support. That would make the חכמים's harsh rejection hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Who stands with him, who holds like him

phrases.english: But there is Ben Beteira
who holds like him!
As we learned in a mishna:
Ben Beteira permits selling a horse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא בֶּן בְּתִירָא דְּקָאֵי כְּוָותֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים's rejection in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נחום המדי's horse ruling is 'forgotten'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view held by a תנא in a משנה cannot be called forgotten; בן בתירא seems to hold like נחום המדי.

steps.title: נחום המדי really holds like the רבנן, not like בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: בן בתירא permits every horse, but נחום המדי only permits a male one. So נחום המדי basically agrees with the רבנן who forbid horses, and the רבנן reject even his small exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן בתירא does not make a difference between males and females. Since נחום המדי does make a difference between males and females, he holds like the רבנן. And according to the רבנן, the matter should be forgotten and not said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בן בתירא and נחום המדי are not really saying the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בתירא allows selling any horse, male or female. נחום המדי only allows a male, which shows he accepts the רבנן's basic ban on selling horses and just makes a narrow exception. Within the רבנן's own view, that exception is rejected, so it can be called forgotten.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think נחום המדי is a more lenient version of בן בתירא. He is actually on the strict side, with the רבנן, and only makes one small exception.

phrases.english: Ben Beteira does not distinguish
between males and females;
he, since he does distinguish
phrases.notes: 'He' here means נחום המדי.

phrases.english: between males and females,
holds like the Rabbis.
And according to the Rabbis,
let the matter be forgotten and not be said.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן בְּתִירָא לָא מְפַלֵּיג בֵּין זְכָרִים לִנְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the opinions: the supposed supporter actually holds a different view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נחום המדי and בן בתירא both permit selling horses, so his view is supported.
steps.terutzMaskana: נחום המדי works within the רבנן's ban, and within that view his exception is rejected.

steps.title: נחום המדי says dill is tithed in all its parts
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: נחום המדי says dill must be tithed as seed, vegetable, and pods. The חכמים say it should be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: נחום המדי says dill is tithed as seed, as vegetable, and as pods. They said to him: let this matter be forgotten and not be said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ruling of נחום המדי, this time about מעשרות, which the חכמים also rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחום המדי holds that every part of the dill plant that people eat needs מעשר: the seeds, the leaves, and the pods. The חכמים reject this. The same pattern as before is about to repeat.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets was added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Nachum the Mede says:
Dill is tithed
as seed, as vegetable, and as pods.
They said to him:
Let the matter be forgotten and not be said!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ, נַחוּם הַמָּדִי אוֹמֵר: הַשֶּׁבֶת מִתְעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another example of a rejected ruling of נחום המדי, parallel to step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחום המדי holds dill needs מעשר as seed, vegetable, and pods; the חכמים reject it.

steps.title: But רבי אליעזר says the same thing about dill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a משנה quotes רבי אליעזר saying exactly what נחום המדי said, so how can it be called forgotten?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is רבי אליעזר who agrees with him, as we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says dill is tithed as seed, vegetable, and pods!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'forgotten' label again, because רבי אליעזר in a משנה says the very same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge is even stronger than the horse one, because רבי אליעזר's wording is almost identical to נחום המדי's. If a תנא in a משנה holds this view, it cannot be forgotten.

phrases.english: But there is Rabbi Eliezer
who holds like him!
As we learned in a mishna:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Dill is tithed
as seed, as vegetable, and as pods!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּקָאֵי כְּוָותֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 17, in the same way step 15 challenged step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נחום המדי's dill ruling is 'forgotten'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר in a משנה states the identical ruling, so the view has support.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is talking about garden dill
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר speaks only about garden dill. נחום המדי seems to include all dill, and that is what was rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, רבי אליעזר is talking about garden dill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר is talking about a different kind of dill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garden dill is good enough that people eat all its parts, so all of them need מעשר. נחום המדי's ruling is not limited to garden dill, and that wider ruling is what the חכמים rejected. So רבי אליעזר does not really support him.

phrases.english: There, it is speaking about the garden kind.
phrases.notes: 'There' means רבי אליעזר's משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בִּדְגִנּוּנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the supporting source is about a narrower case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר and נחום המדי hold the same ruling about all dill.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר speaks only about garden dill, so נחום המדי's wider ruling stays rejected.

steps.title: רב אחא complains that the great man from his land is always rejected
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר מניומי tells אביי: a great man came from our homeland, and everything he said is answered with 'let it be forgotten.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר מניומי said to אביי: A great man came from our place, and every thing he said, they say to him: 'Let the matter be forgotten and not be said.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא, who came from the same land as נחום המדי, complains that all of his rulings are being rejected. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After three rejected rulings in a row, רב אחא is bothered: is nothing this great sage said accepted? His words work like a question that asks whether any ruling of נחום המדי survives.

keyTerms.meaning: From our place, from our homeland

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Minyomi said to Abaye:
A great man came from our place,
phrases.notes: He means נחום המדי, who came from Media, the same land as רב אחא.

phrases.english: and every thing that he said,
they say to him:
'Let the matter be forgotten and not be said.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the individual rulings and reacts to the overall pattern of rejection.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there any ruling of נחום המדי that is actually followed?

steps.title: אביי: we do follow נחום המדי on asking for needs in שומע תפלה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that there is one ruling of נחום המדי we follow: a person may ask for his personal needs in the ברכה of שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: There is one ruling that we act like him, as it is taught: נחום המדי says a person may ask for his needs in 'שומע תפלה'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב אחא's complaint by pointing to one ruling of נחום המדי that is accepted in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argues that not everything נחום המדי said was rejected. His ruling that a person may add his own personal requests in the ברכה of שומע תפלה in the עמידה is followed in practice. The next step challenges whether this really counts as נחום המדי's own ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: That we act like him, follow him in practice
'Who hears prayer,' the ending of a ברכה in the עמידה

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים rejected several rulings of נחום המדי, and each time another תנא who seemed to agree turned out to hold something different. אביי points to one ruling we do follow, asking for personal needs in שומע תפלה. The next step argues that even this cannot be credited to נחום המדי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה still followed today: personal requests may be added in the ברכה of שומע תפלה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering. The word in square brackets was added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: There is one ruling
in which we act like him,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Nachum the Mede says:
A person may ask for his needs
in 'Who hears prayer.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיכָּא חֲדָא דְּעָבְדִינַן כְּוָותֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. We follow נחום המדי's ruling that a person may ask for personal needs in שומע תפלה.

steps.title: This ruling does not prove anything about נחום המדי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר מניומי says the example אביי gave does not count, because that ruling already depends on a dispute between great Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave out that one, because it depends on great trees, meaning great Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר מניומי rejects אביי's example. He says the ruling about personal requests is not really something new from נחום המדי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי tried to show that at least one ruling of נחום המדי was accepted. רב אחא answers that this idea was already argued about by earlier, greater Sages. So following it does not show that נחום המדי himself was ever accepted, and no ruling original to him has been shown to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: apart from it, leave it out
it depends on, it hangs on
great trees, a picture for great Sages

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not saying the הלכה about personal requests is wrong. He is only saying it cannot be credited to נחום המדי.

phrases.english: He said [to him]: Apart from that one,
phrases.notes: This is רב אחא בר מניומי answering אביי. Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: which depends on great trees.
phrases.notes: 'Great trees' is a picture for great Sages, who are about to be named.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה בר מינה דההיא דתליא באשלי רברבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the שומע תפלה ruling as proof that נחום המדי was ever followed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling comes from an older dispute between greater Sages, so it is not a ruling original to נחום המדי.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: ask for your needs first, then pray
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the earlier dispute. רבי אליעזר holds that a person asks for his needs first and prays afterward, and he brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says a person asks for his needs and afterward prays. The פסוק says 'A prayer of the afflicted when he is faint, and before ה׳ he pours out his שיחה.' And שיחה always means prayer, as the פסוק says 'And יצחק went out לשוח in the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that backs up רב אחא's claim. It opens with the opinion of רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the poor man's suffering, which is his request, comes first, and only after that does he pour out his שיחה. A second פסוק about יצחק proves that שיחה means prayer. So the order is: requests first, then prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: speech before God, which here means prayer
to speak with God, to pray

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person requests his needs
and afterward he prays,
as it says: "A prayer of the poor man when he is faint
phrases.notes: תהלים 102:1

phrases.english: and before ה׳ he pours out his speech, etc.",
and 'speech' means nothing other than prayer,
as it says: "And Yitzchak went out to speak [with God] in the field."
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:63

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא רבי אליעזר אומר שואל אדם צרכיו ואחר כך יתפלל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that proves step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that personal requests in prayer were already argued about by great Sages.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר, who reads תהלים 102:1 together with the פסוק about יצחק.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: pray first, then ask for your needs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע holds the opposite order: pray first, and only afterward ask for personal needs. He brings a different פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: A person prays, and afterward he asks for his needs, as the פסוק says, 'I pour out my שיחה before Him, I tell my trouble before Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the other side of the dispute, the opinion of רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהושע's פסוק, pouring out שיחה, which is prayer, comes first. Telling one's trouble, which is the request, comes after it. So his order is the reverse of רבי אליעזר's.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds: requests first, then prayer. רבי יהושע holds: prayer first, then requests. Each one has his own פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: He prays,
and afterward he requests his needs,
as it says: "I pour out my speech before Him,
phrases.notes: תהלים 142:3

phrases.english: I tell my trouble before Him."

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יהושע אומר יתפלל ואחר כך ישאל צרכיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First pray, then ask for personal needs.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר do with רבי יהושע's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר: the פסוק 'I pour out my שיחה before Him' seems to put prayer first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי אליעזר too, isn't it written, 'I pour out my שיחה before Him'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר can hold his view when רבי יהושע's פסוק seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That פסוק names pouring out שיחה, which is prayer, before telling one's trouble, which is the request. This looks like a direct contradiction to רבי אליעזר's order.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer as well,
isn't it written: "I pour out my speech before Him"!

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי אליעזר נמי הכתיב אשפך לפניו שיחי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר using רבי יהושע's פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that requests come first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word order of תהלים 142:3 puts prayer before telling one's trouble.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as 'once I have told my trouble'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains the פסוק to mean: I pour out my prayer at the time when I have already told my trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: I pour out my שיחה before Him once I have told my trouble before Him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אליעזר by reading the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the פסוק is read as the condition for the first half. The prayer is poured out after the trouble has been told. So the request still comes first, just as רבי אליעזר said.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying: "I pour out my speech before Him"
at the time when I have told my trouble before Him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכי קאמר אשפוך לפניו שיחי בזמן שצרתי לפניו אגיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק a new way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's word order shows that prayer comes first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means prayer is poured out after the trouble has already been told.

steps.title: What does רבי יהושע do with רבי אליעזר's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע: the פסוק 'A prayer of the poor man when he is faint' seems to put the request first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יהושע too, isn't it written, 'A prayer of the poor man when he is faint'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the same question around and asks it against רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים 102 mentions the poor man's distress before the pouring out of שיחה. That seems to put the request before the prayer, which goes against רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua as well,
isn't it written: "A prayer of the poor man when he is faint"!

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יהושע נמי הכתיב תפלה לעני כי יעטף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 25, now aimed at רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's view that prayer comes first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word order of תהלים 102:1 puts the poor man's request before pouring out שיחה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע reads the פסוק as 'once he has prayed'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע explains: the poor man's request is accepted only once he has already poured out his prayer before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: When is there a prayer for the poor man? At the time when he has already poured out his שיחה before ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהושע by reading the פסוק so it fits his order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the פסוק, pouring out שיחה, becomes the condition for the first half, the poor man's request. Prayer comes first, and only then is the request in place. This matches רבי יהושע.
steps.whatToRemember: Each Sage reads the other's פסוק as a 'when' sentence. The second half of the פסוק becomes the condition that must happen first. This lets each Sage keep his own order.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying: When is there a prayer for the poor man?
At the time when he has poured out his speech before ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכי קאמר אימתי תפלה לעני בזמן שלפני ה׳ ישפוך שיחו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק a new way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's word order shows that the request comes first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The poor man's request comes only after he has poured out his prayer.

steps.title: The verses cannot settle it, so what is the real dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the פסוקים fit neither רבי אליעזר nor רבי יהושע exactly, and asks what their disagreement really depends on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, the פסוקים do not clearly fit this Sage, and they do not clearly fit that Sage. So what do they really disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees that each Sage was able to explain away the other's פסוק, so the פסוקים prove nothing. It asks what the argument is truly based on, setting up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 25-28, each פסוק that seemed to support one side was explained so it also fits the other side. Since the פסוקים can be read either way, they cannot be the real reason for the dispute. The גמרא now looks for an underlying idea that divides them.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since it is clear that (introduces a reasoning step)
They fit precisely; they can be read exactly that way

phrases.english: Now, the verses
do not fit precisely like this Master
phrases.notes: Each מר points to one of the two Sages here: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: and do not fit precisely like that Master,
about what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי קְרָאֵי לָא כְּמָר דָּיְיקִי וְלָא כְּמָר דָּיְיקִי, בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the challenge-and-answer exchange of Steps 25-28: neither side's פסוק is decisive, so the גמרא asks for the true basis of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying idea or principle divides רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, since the פסוקים do not decide it?

steps.title: The dispute depends on רבי שמלאי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the disagreement relates to רבי שמלאי's teaching that a person should first praise ה׳ and only then pray for his needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about what רבי שמלאי taught. רבי שמלאי taught: A person should always first set out the praise of ה׳, and only afterward pray for his needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 29 by pointing to a teaching of רבי שמלאי. That teaching says praise of ה׳ must come before personal requests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a פסוק, the dispute now rests on a principle about the order of prayer: praise first, requests after. The order 'pray first, then ask for needs' (רבי יהושע's view) matches this principle, while רבי אליעזר's order, putting personal needs first, does not.

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יתפלל' means praying for one's own needs, while the praise of ה׳ is what comes first.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always first praise ה׳ and only afterward pray for his own needs.

steps.title: Proof from משה רבינו: praise first, then the request
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי שמלאי's rule and brings it from משה רבינו, who first praised ה׳ and in the next פסוק asked to enter the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From משה רבינו. It is written: 'ה׳ God, You have begun to show Your servant...' (praise). And right after it is written: 'Let me cross over, please, and see the good land' (request).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי שמלאי's rule comes from, and proves it from the order of two פסוקים in דברים. משה praised ה׳ first and only then made his request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from order: the praise in one פסוק is followed by the request in the very next פסוק. Since משה רבינו prayed this way, it serves as the model for everyone: praise first, then personal requests.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

steps.whatToRemember: The order of prayer is praise of ה׳ first, then personal requests, learned from משה רבינו in דברים פרק ג. This principle is the real basis of the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the basis for the structure of תפלה: we begin with praise of ה׳ before asking for our needs.
